Formulation
- Brief summary: Precipitating factor is a new, stressful job; current symptoms include persistent anxiety, sleep disturbance, low mood, and somatic palpitations. Perpetuating factors include sleep disruption, avoidance of social/activities, potential caffeine/alcohol use, and ongoing work-related stress. Protective factors include family support and willingness to engage in care. No acute suicidality or violence risk identified.

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Address each principal problem identified in Clinical Assessment - Section A. Add additional problems as relevant.)

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce anxiety to enable leaving home and attending work
  - Improve sleep quality and daytime energy
  - Re-engage in social activities and hobbies
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Access and engage in evidence-based therapy (talking therapy)
  - Implement sleep hygiene and monitoring for insomnia
  - Evaluate and monitor palpitations; arrange basic medical tests if indicated
  - Provide information/resources for self-management; plan for stepwise escalation if needed
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT/related)
  - Use online resources and self-help tools for anxiety
  - Attend arranged blood tests for palpitations and follow-up
  - Practice sleep hygiene and gradual re-engagement with activities
  - Contact GP if anxiety worsens or daily functioning declines
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Initiate referral to NHS talking therapy; provide links/resources
  - Provide sleep hygiene guidance and monitoring resources
  - Arrange basic blood tests to evaluate palpitations; arrange follow-up with results in about one week
  - Offer ongoing monitoring and consider pharmacotherapy if symptoms escalate (discussion noted; not initiated initially)
  - Document plan and ensure access to online self-help resources

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve sleep quality and daytime functioning
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Target insomnia symptoms and maintain mood stability
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue sleep hygiene practices; maintain regular routines; resume enjoyable activities as tolerated
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide sleep-related education/resources; assess need for Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I) if needed; monitor mood and energy

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes

- Coping Strategies:
